record_heading: Shared answers (every record points here)
text: **Splits and production findings that apply to several records** (each on its own line where it first matters): - SPLIT-A: the rule "where a press's own end sits once the game's read end is X" is held twice. `tools/ch_probe/experiments/play_chart.py:361-369` (`own_end_now_ms`) picks the early or late ratio by comparing the read with `read_stored_end_ms`. `tools/replay_schedule.cpp:273-276` (`read_at_own_ms`) solves the same sum backwards and picks the ratio by comparing the own end with `own_stored_end_ms`; its comment at 271-272 says it is "the player's sum, solved for the read". Two code paths for one rule; nothing I read ties them together on a real chart. Records 62, 79, 88, 89 and 90 rest on it. - FINDING-B: `play_chart.py:111` `SCORE_READ_DELAY_S = 0.005` and `:115` `RUN_CAP_S = 240.0` are numbers with a comment pointing at a spike plan, not a rule (record 9, record 18). - FINDING-C: message text and unit spacing differ between stop reasons: `play_chart.py:777-778` writes "the clock at 200.00s", while the frozen stop (from `live.py`, not read) is quoted by the test as "clock frozen at 20.00 s" (record 111).
